intro: Before giving you the code, the full Code T pipeline was run in GNU Octave for the crowded case with the final settings (power control, 10-dB clusters, stretched arrays), with 2 random drops and 200 symbols (25,600 bits per point, so values below about 4x10-4 rest on fewer than 10 errors and are noisy). Cross-AP List BER:
comment: What this shows (2 drops only, not final results): (1) the proposed Cross-AP List detector now gives a real waterfall over 0-24 dB; the sparse arrays are at about 5x10-4 to 1.5x10-3 at 20 dB, so 10-4 is reached between 20 and 28 dB (the SNR grid now goes to 28 dB). (2) The dense λ/2 ULA falls much more slowly (no near-field links, tiny aperture). (3) Co-array processing changes nothing measurable: the results were identical in 43-50 % of the (SNR, drop) points and the rest differ only by noise. (4) Linear MMSE and List SIC still floor at about 0.1-0.16 with 16-QAM: the larger clusters lowered the floor but did not remove it. QPSK was also tested (1 drop): all detectors then reach zero errors by 4-8 dB, so the 0-20 dB region is empty and no waterfall is visible. That is why Code T uses 16-QAM. If the professor needs 10-4 exactly at 20 dB, it should come from the system (for example more antennas per AP or fewer users), not from redefining the SNR axis.
